Hard to keep my attention on one thing? Yeah, I guess that happens a lot. Like, I can start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine, you know, checking the tickets against the garments. Act on impulse? No, I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, I don't just go out and buy a new car on a whim or anything crazy like that. I'm pretty sensible.

Smaller steps? Hmm, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if that helps or not. I suppose it might? But I usually just try to tackle things as they come.

Oh, my goodness, Doctor, I think you might be asking me the same thing again! But yes, absolutely. It's exactly like I was just saying. If I'm working on something for a while, my focus just packs up and leaves. 

I'll sit down with the dry-cleaning orders, and I'm totally fine at first. But a few minutes go by, and suddenly I'm not looking at the tickets anymore. I'm staring at the care labels and wondering who invented the little symbols, or I'm planning out the hymns for Sunday service, or I'm worrying about whether I left a window open at the house. She just likes having them fresh in the closet, I suppose. Grief does funny things to people. When my mother passed, I couldn't stop baking. I'll snap out of thinking about Mrs. Higgins' Buick or whatever, and I'll realize I've completely missed half the tickets I was supposed to be checking. It just gets so much harder to pay attention the longer I do it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your difficulty in focusing and completing tasks is causing significant problems in your daily life or relationships?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, I suppose it is causing some real headaches. At the shop, it's gotten pretty bad. We've had late orders because I lose track of time, and the billing... oh, the billing gets so confused when I'm trying to sort it out. I've had some really tense moments with the staff and even a few customers. It reminds me of this one lady, Mrs. Gable, she came in last Thursday looking for her husband's tuxedo. He had this big gala for the Rotary Club. They always do it at that fancy hotel downtown, the one with the big crystal chandeliers in the lobby. I went to a wedding there once, back in the eighties. The bride wore this dress with the biggest puffed sleeves you've ever seen, it looked like she had two white pumpkins on her shoulders. Her mother insisted on a chocolate fountain, which was a terrible idea because halfway through the reception, the groom's uncle—who had a bit too much champagne, mind you—bumped the table and chocolate went everywhere. It took them hours to clean the carpet, and I don't think they ever got the stain out of the bride's train...\n\nOh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yes, it's causing problems. Even at church, I've had to step back from leading some of the planning committees. People were just getting too frustrated with me forgetting things and getting off track. My grandmother used to hide her bourbon in an empty vanilla extract bottle in the pantry so my grandfather wouldn't drink it.
